solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Nice request to perform on stage?

parts.note: a plea is an earnest request
to sing is to perform as a vocalist on stage

explanation.surface: A polite request to get up and do a turn in the theatre.
explanation.definitionFit: Something nice is agreeable to experience, which is a plain synonym.

clue.text: Sharp shower? Hide with little hesitation

parts.note: a pelt is an animal's hide
er is the small sound of hesitating

explanation.surface: Asking about a brief downpour, then hiding with a short pause.
explanation.definitionFit: A heavy, driving downpour is called this in British usage, a sudden burst of rain.

clue.text: English university enjoyable for a girl

parts.note: nice means pleasant or enjoyable

explanation.surface: An English college that's fun for a young woman.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a female first name, so the definition is by example.

clue.text: Authorise punitive action

definitions.meaning: a penalty, such as trade restrictions imposed on a country

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both official approval and a penalty, a contradiction in one word.

clue.text: Architect establishing name with a second hospital

parts.note: H abbreviates hospital on road signs

explanation.surface: A designer setting up a further hospital.
explanation.walkthrough: John Nash designed Regent Street and the Brighton Pavilion; 'establishing' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: John Nash was a Regency architect, so the definition is by example.

clue.text: Lacking debt, as young whelp receiving help

indicators.note: the young dog takes in the help, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: a pup is a young dog, a whelp
aid means help

explanation.surface: A debt-free person compared with a puppy being given assistance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'receiving' signals the container; 'as' is only a link, and 'young whelp' reads as part of the picture.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone whose dues are fully settled owes nothing, so is free of debt.

clue.text: A public vehicle can accommodate a hundred — you can count on that

indicators.note: the vehicle is able to hold the hundred inside it

parts.note: a bus is public transport
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, with A for a

explanation.surface: A bus has room for a hundred people, and you can rely on it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can accommodate' signals the container. The definition plays on the idiom 'count on', meaning rely on.
explanation.definitionFit: A frame of beads is used for counting, so you literally count on it.

clue.text: Relocate short parade before church

indicators.note: the cut word comes ahead of the church piece
the word is cut short, losing its last letter

parts.note: to parade is to display or show off
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: Moving a truncated procession to the front of a church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' trims DISPLAY to DISPLA.
explanation.definitionFit: To move something from its place is to relocate it, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Despair unusual round a land of bliss

indicators.note: the shuffled letters go around the next piece
the letters of the word are put into an unusual order

explanation.surface: Unusual despair surrounding a place of happiness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusual' rearranges DESPAIR and 'round' wraps those letters about A.
explanation.definitionFit: Heaven or Eden is a place of perfect happiness, a land of bliss.

clue.text: Communist register includes a number heading west

indicators.note: the register takes the turned number inside it, a container signal

parts.note: a list is a register or roll

indicators.note: in an across clue, going west means reading right to left, so the number is turned round

parts.note: nine is a number

explanation.surface: A party roll that has some figure moving leftwards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heading west' gives the reversal, since across entries read west to east; 'includes' is the container.
explanation.definitionFit: A follower of Lenin's doctrine is a kind of Communist, so the noun fits by example.

clue.text: Conqueror could create a scare

indicators.note: the letters of the following words could be rearranged to create something new

explanation.surface: A warlord is capable of frightening people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could create' tells you to rearrange A SCARE.
explanation.definitionFit: Julius of Rome conquered Gaul, so he is a famous conqueror; the name also became a title for emperors.

clue.text: Eleanor, perhaps the last character to get sun-tanned

parts.note: Eleanor Bron is a British actress and writer
zed is the letter Z, last of the alphabet

explanation.surface: Eleanor, maybe, getting a tan in the end.
explanation.walkthrough: Eleanor Bron is an English actress, known from the Beatles film Help!; 'to get' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Skin turned brown by the sun has a metal-like colour, a synonym for tanned.

clue.text: Old lover getting mention brings thrill

parts.note: an ex is a former partner
to cite is to mention or refer to

explanation.surface: A former partner being named in conversation is a source of excitement.
explanation.definitionFit: To thrill someone is to stir them up, a verb synonym; 'brings' is a link.

clue.text: Worried Irish politician holding money in Russia

indicators.note: the politician grips the money, so it goes inside

parts.note: TD stands for Teachta Dala, a member of the Irish parliament
the rouble is the Russian currency

explanation.surface: An anxious Irish politician with Russian cash on him.
explanation.walkthrough: TD (Teachta Dala) is a member of the Dail, Ireland's lower house; 'holding' signals the container.
explanation.definitionFit: Troubled and worried both describe someone uneasy and anxious, a straight synonym.

clue.text: Tot, one boy to become a writer

parts.note: to tot up is to add
I is the Roman numeral one
a son is a boy

explanation.surface: A child and another boy grow up to be an author.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tot' looks like a small child but is the verb 'tot up'. 'to become' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Joseph Addison was an 18th-century essayist who founded The Spectator, so a writer by example.

clue.text: Excuse trick performed

parts.note: a con is a trick or swindle
done means carried out or performed

explanation.surface: Forgiving a confidence trick that has been carried out.
explanation.definitionFit: To overlook or forgive an offence is to excuse it, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Book agreements not needing introductory page

indicators.note: the word for agreements does without a letter, so it is removed

parts.note: pacts are agreements or treaties
p, the first letter of page and its usual abbreviation

explanation.surface: Contracts in a volume that can skip the opening page.
explanation.walkthrough: The book is the Acts of the Apostles in the New Testament; 'not needing' removes P from PACTS.
explanation.definitionFit: Acts of the Apostles is a book of the Bible, so the definition is by example.

clue.text: Twisty stuff put on cheap jewellery

parts.note: to ram is to stuff or cram
bling is flashy, showy jewellery

explanation.surface: Something winding wrapped in gaudy trinkets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put on' places the first piece on top of the second in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A rambling road meanders, so the word can describe something winding and twisty.

clue.text: Space not properly allocated for top bit of structure

indicators.note: the letters are allotted into their proper order, a sign to rearrange

explanation.surface: A space that has not been correctly assigned for the summit of a building.
explanation.walkthrough: 'properly allocated' rearranges SPACE and NOT; 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The finishing stone set at the top of a wall or building is its crowning piece.

clue.text: Maiden? Funny performer not half emotional

parts.note: in cricket a maiden is an over with no runs scored

indicators.note: only half the word is kept, the second half removed

parts.note: a comedian is a funny performer

explanation.surface: A young woman? A comedian only half moved.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, a maiden is an over of six balls with no runs. 'not half' cuts COMEDIAN to COME.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone overcome is overwhelmed by feeling, so emotional by synonym.

clue.text: First gardener to make an embankment

parts.note: a dam is a barrier or embankment holding back water

explanation.surface: The original gardener of Eden building a bank.
explanation.walkthrough: Genesis puts the first man in charge of the Garden of Eden; 'to make' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis the first man tends the Garden of Eden, so he is the first gardener.

clue.text: Some examiner valued as a wise female

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: An examiner prized as a woman of wisdom.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'as' into the definition; it is a link word, since 'as a wise female' cannot stand for a name.
explanation.definitionFit: The Roman goddess of wisdom is the wise female figure of mythology.

clue.text: Capone was dishonest in partnership

parts.note: Al Capone, the Chicago gangster
lied means told untruths

explanation.surface: The gangster Capone cheated his business associates.
explanation.definitionFit: Allied parties are joined in an alliance, which is a partnership.

clue.text: Vegetable rubbish under vehicle

indicators.note: in a down clue the rubbish sits below the vehicle

parts.note: a car is a vehicle
rot means nonsense or rubbish

explanation.surface: Vegetable refuse lying beneath a car.
explanation.definitionFit: An orange root crop is a common vegetable, so the definition is by example.

clue.text: Character who makes provision for tenants?

definitions.meaning: a landlord, one who lets property to renters

explanation.definitionFit: It is both an alphabet symbol and, whimsically, one who lets property.

clue.text: Two men meeting somewhere in Essex

parts.note: Basil is a man's name
Don is another man's name

explanation.surface: Two men getting together at a place in Essex.
explanation.walkthrough: Essex is a county east of London; Basildon is one of its towns. 'meeting' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A town in the English county of Essex, so the definition is by example.

clue.text: Oil film

definitions.meaning: to oil is to lubricate, apply lubricant to a machine
a 1978 musical film starring John Travolta

explanation.definitionFit: To lubricate with fat is to oil; the word also titles the 1978 Travolta musical.

clue.text: Understood part of play through earphones

indicators.note: words heard through earphones are taken by their sound

parts.note: a scene is a division of a play

explanation.surface: Grasping part of a drama listened to on headphones.
explanation.walkthrough: 'through earphones' means you hear SCENE, which sounds the same as the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: If something has been grasped it is understood, in the sense 'I see'.

clue.text: One mathematical shape of holy symbol?

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
a conic is a curve made by slicing a cone, a shape in mathematics

explanation.surface: A single geometric figure belonging to a religious emblem.
explanation.definitionFit: An icon is a holy image, so something relating to an icon is described by this adjective.

clue.text: Protest about despicable person, American politician

parts.note: a demo is a protest march
c is short for circa, about
a rat is a despicable, treacherous person

explanation.surface: Demonstrating against a contemptible US politician.
explanation.definitionFit: A member of one of the two main US parties is an American politician, by example.

clue.text: Eager journalist with drab clothing

indicators.note: the drab colour dresses the journalist, wrapping round it

parts.note: grey means dull or drab
ED is short for editor, a journalist

explanation.surface: A keen reporter dressed in dull clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clothing' signals the container; 'with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Eager for more, wanting a lot, is a sense of being grasping or avid.

clue.text: Rose can't work out who might be great-grandmother?

indicators.note: the letters are worked out into a fresh arrangement

parts.note: the apostrophe drops away, leaving the letters as written

explanation.surface: A woman named Rose fails to figure out who her great-grandmother was.
explanation.walkthrough: 'work out' shuffles ROSE and CANT; 'Rose' looks like a name or verb but is only letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A great-grandmother is one example of a forebear, hence the question mark.
